newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-NO CHANGE AFTER VALENCIA-BARCELONA DRAW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-NO CHANGE AFTER VALENCIA-BARCELONA DRAW.

text.p: Barcelona's action-packed 1-1 draw with Valencia on Sunday was enough to keep their faint title hopes alive as Real Madrid could only manage the same result at Tenerife.
Bobby Robson's side also held on to second place on goal difference from Real Betis who drew 0-0 at Espanyol.
It also meant Valencia maintained their unbeaten home record and eased the pressure on coach Jorge Valdano -- for now.

Valdano denied that he had been warned to get a result "or else". But few could doubt that chairman Paco Roig would tolerate many more weeks without seeing a change in the fortunes of a club among the league's biggest pre-season spenders.
The lack of success has already cost the job of Valdano's predecessor, Luis Aragones, but the club remains firmly entrenched in mid-table with little chance of a UEFA Cup place.

Several experienced Valencia commentators say the Argentine now seems to have turned a corner and looked far more relaxed in Sunday's post-match conference than at any time previously in his four months at the Mestalla stadium.
Valdano's calm came after his team had weathered an early Barcelona storm.
Ronaldo missed two good early opportunities -- "it's difficult to take a chance in the first two minutes," said Robson -- but the Brazilian was seen nursing a leg injury after one of the efforts.
Valencia's success in containing the visitors was aided by the problems of a man who had scored a scintillating hat-trick in Barcelona's 3-2 victory over Valencia earlier this season.
Despite the injury, Ronaldo knocked in the equaliser and then flew to Brazil to play for his country in a friendly.
There is a growing feeling in Spain that regular trips back to Brazil -- one a well-publicised visit to the Rio carnival -- may prove decisive in the striker's future.
Barcelona are thought to be considering accepting an offer from Italy's Lazio which would allow them to sign Real Madrid teenager Raul Gonzalez and Real Betis striker Alfonso Perez.
The Spanish league lost around 50 foreign players to World Cup games over the weekend and teams may begin to place greater emphasis on securing top-class Spaniards like Raul and Alfonso.
Neither man was on target on Sunday but Real's point keeps Barca nine points adrift with 11 games left.
And Betis are keeping the pressure on from below in the battle for Spain's second European Cup place.
Barcelona are desperate to qualify for the cup after going two seasons without a taste of the continent's premier tournament.
Ironically, a man who helped the club win the trophy for the only time, in 1992, was the centre of attention in Sunday's game.
Goalkeeper Andoni Zubizarreta earned praise from all quarters for keeping Valencia afloat by denying his former team mates with several good saves.
But the veteran international was also blamed for allowing a Hristo Stoichkov cross to reach Ronaldo for the equaliser.
